title: Things
question: What am I?
description: Something is talking to you and won't say what it is.

entries.name: The Aral Sea
entries.voiceNote: Asked if it is alive: "I was. Less every year." Dry, literally and otherwise; blames cotton without naming rivers.
mostFamous: shrank to a fraction of itself

entries.name: Voyager 1
entries.voiceNote: Faint, patient, farther away every second; speaks of a record it carries and a photograph it took, and of a very long silence.

entries.name: The Library of Alexandria
entries.era: c. 3rd century BC – c. 3rd century AD
entries.voiceNote: Grieving and grand; will not settle on who burned it because the historians never did; talks about scrolls confiscated from ships.

entries.name: The Antikythera mechanism
entries.voiceNote: Corroded, smug about being two thousand years early; counts eclipses to avoid answering; found by sponge divers and says so proudly.

entries.name: The Rosetta Stone
entries.voiceNote: Says everything three times in three ways and finds that funny; talks about being in the wrong museum.

entries.name: Pompeii
entries.voiceNote: Speaks in the present tense about a lunch that was never finished; mentions the mountain only as "the neighbour".

entries.name: RMS Titanic
entries.voiceNote: Stately, a little defensive about a certain adjective; talks about deck chairs and a band, not about ice.

entries.name: The Colossus of Rhodes
entries.voiceNote: Enormous and brief; toppled by an earthquake and sold for scrap, and still annoyed about the straddling-the-harbour myth.

entries.name: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon
entries.era: described from c. 290 BC; never located
entries.voiceNote: May never have existed and knows it; speaks entirely from hearsay about itself, lush and unverifiable.

entries.name: The Berlin Wall
entries.voiceNote: Concrete and unrepentant, then suddenly in pieces on people's shelves; talks about a night in November without saying which city.

entries.name: Sputnik 1
entries.voiceNote: Small, shiny, proud of having beeped for three weeks and frightened a continent; burned up and thinks that was a fine ending.

entries.name: Concorde
entries.voiceNote: Elegant, expensive, faintly bored by subsonic questions; talks about arriving before it left, not about the noise.
mostFamous: London to New York in under four hours

entries.name: Carthage
entries.voiceNote: Mercantile, sardonic, tired of a certain senator's catchphrase; talks about ships and purple dye, not about who destroyed it.

entries.name: The Great Fire of London
entries.voiceNote: Speaks for four days only and knows it; began in a bakery it will not name; oddly proud of the city that came after.
